V.rationale: Visa is a high-quality, capital-light payments franchise with exceptional margins (net margin ~52%, operating margin ~61%, ROE ~62-65%) and strong revenue growth (+17% YoY in Q2 2026). The business benefits from durable structural tailwinds: global cash-to-digital migration, cross-border travel recovery, and expanding value-added services (VAS now ~30% of revenue, growing 27%). Revenue has grown consistently from $9.5B to $11.2B over the last five reported quarters. However, the stock is not cheap on an absolute basis (P/E ~28.7x, P/S ~14.8x, P/B ~16.8x) and has underperformed over the past year (-7% to -10% YTD), partly reflecting regulatory overhang (CCCA, DOJ antitrust, EU interchange rulings) and Berkshire Hathaway's full exit from the position. The stock sits ~15% below its 52-week high of $375.51, which offers some valuation relief vs. recent history, but the multiple remains elevated relative to the broader market. Near-term catalysts are modest: the stablecoin settlement pilot with Brale (June 4 news) and the Q3 earnings report (July 28) could provide positive re-rating if guidance is maintained or raised. The stablecoin initiative is strategically interesting but still early-stage. Overall, this is a strong franchise at a fair-to-slightly-rich valuation with manageable but real regulatory risks, warranting a mildly positive score.
